title: Dealer Locator Test
featureSummary: Verifies the homepage-to-dealer-locator-to-results flow (Find Dealers link, top-cities list, dealer results page), plus a comment-raised question about whether the results sort control actually reorders results.

acceptanceCriteria.requirement: Clicking "Find Dealers" from the homepage navigates to the dealer locator page
The dealer locator page shows a top-cities list with at least 5 cities
Selecting a city reaches a results page (DRP) showing more than one dealer, each with name, address, and a CTA

commentScenarios.summary: Does the sort/filter option on the dealer results page actually reorder the results, or just visually open?
commentScenarios.notes: Confirmed the sort panel does functionally reorder results, not just open cosmetically.

scenarios.name: Dealer locator page loads with its core elements
steps: Waited for the top-cities list to render
scenarios.expected: Dealer locator page renders with heading, city/zip search input, map, and top-cities list
scenarios.actual: Page rendered "Dealer locator for car tires" heading, search input placeholder "Enter a city, suburb, town or zip code", and top-cities list, within ~4ms of the wait resolving

scenarios.name: AC-1 — Find Dealers link from the homepage navigates to the dealer locator page
scenarios.expected: Browser navigates to the dealer locator page (/auto/dealer-locator)
scenarios.actual: Navigation succeeded — the dealer-locator-only elements (".dl__top-cities-list") appeared immediately after the click with no error

scenarios.name: AC-2 — Top-cities list shows at least 5 cities
steps: On the dealer locator page, inspected the top-cities list
scenarios.actual: Exactly 5 cities present: Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles, New-York — meets the "at least 5" requirement with no headroom above it

scenarios.name: AC-3 — Selecting a city reaches a results page with more than one dealer, each with name/address/CTA
steps: Waited for dealer result cards to render
scenarios.expected: Results page shows >1 dealer, each with a name, address, and a CTA
scenarios.actual: "566 car tire dealers in Atlanta, GA, USA" heading; first two cards (MIDAS, GORDY TIRE AND AUTOMOTIVE) each show a name, distance/address line, and a "Contact dealer" CTA

scenarios.name: Comment — Does the sort control actually reorder dealer results, or just visually open?
steps: On the Atlanta results page, read the first card title under the default "Sort by: Recommended" state ("MIDAS")
Clicked "Sort by" to open the panel — confirmed options: Recommended, Distance, Name, Number of reviews, Best reviews
Re-read the first card title after the selection
scenarios.expected: Selecting a sort option changes the actual order of the result cards, not just the label on the control
scenarios.actual: First card changed from "MIDAS" (Recommended) to "4 WHEEL PARTS" (Name, ascending — digit sorts before letters) — the list demonstrably reordered, this is not cosmetic-only

analytics.action: Clicked "Find Dealers", searched/selected a city, and applied a sort selection
analytics.evidence: One first-party request to what appears to be an analytics/logging endpoint (POST-style "https://dctityd.michelinman.com/status-log") fired during the session, but it returned HTTP 400. No GA/GTM/Tealium/Segment request or window.dataLayer instrumentation was checked in this lightweight pass, so this is not a confident PASS — flagged for a follow-up run with explicit dataLayer capture.

observations: None of the console errors or network failures above coincide with, or appear to affect, the Find Dealers navigation, top-cities list, dealer results, or sort behaviour tested in S1–S5 — they are recorded for the record, not filed as bugs against this ticket's ACs.
The 'userLocale' duplicate-declaration pageerror suggests a script is being injected/loaded twice somewhere on the page — worth a developer look, but did not visibly break any tested functionality.

The second, focused recording session (sort verification) observed a similar small number of console errors and network failures of the same apparent origin (chat-widget audio, CSP data: script) — not itemised individually since that session's evidence file was consolidated into this report.

This run intentionally covered only AC-1, AC-2, AC-3 and the sort/filter comment scenario, per an explicit lightweight-first-pass request. The mandatory boundary checklist (10-item, per interactive widget) and the exhaustive regression census (decomposed, executed) were NOT run — see regressionInventory, which lists discovered-but-unexercised widgets only.
warnings: Boundary checklist skipped for this run (user request) — filters, empty/single-result states, invalid input, rapid interaction, URL persistence and back-button behaviour on the dealer locator/results flow remain untested.
Regression census entries below are discovery-only (from the live-DOM census) and are explicitly not decomposed or exercised — see regressionInventory[].result for each.

existingCoverage: features/dealer-locator.feature — 4 scenarios: page load with core elements, city search via autocomplete, dealer card contents (title/address), details-page navigation
missingScenarios: S3 (MEDIUM): Top-cities list has at least 5 cities (exact-count assertion)
S5 (HIGH, declared gap): Selecting a sort option (e.g. Name) actually reorders dealer results, not just opens the panel

missingSteps.step: the first dealer card should change after sorting

automationGap.recommendation: The sort control on the dealer results page (COVERAGE.md's declared gap) works correctly — it demonstrably reorders results — but has zero automated coverage. Adding one step for opening it, one for selecting an option, and one assertion that the first card's title changes would close this gap and match what this run just verified manually.

conclusion: All 3 acceptance criteria met and the sort/filter comment scenario confirmed the control genuinely reorders results (not just a cosmetic panel). Zero bugs found. This was an explicitly reduced first-pass scope — the boundary checklist and full regression census were skipped per request and should follow in a subsequent run.
